final_answer: Implement ATOM_003 as a single, self-contained addition to tools/test-decision-synthesis.ps1: one new function (Test-DepthRoutingAssertion) that wraps one dedicated assertion block, calls Get-SynthesisDepthDecision directly, and asserts the three-pole depth split — Standard / High-Stakes / Deep. The Standard pole is exercised with a plan-refinement DISCUSS fixture that contains NO literal обсуди/discuss/architecture markers, so it is green against the router as it exists today; the High-Stakes pole uses an explicit high-stakes marker; the Deep pole uses a broad architecture/design input. Fixtures are ASCII-only and the Standard case is free of high-risk keywords to avoid accidental router escalation. The block reuses the existing Assert-True / $script:pass / $script:total / exit 1 harness, and the file's existing ParseFile + smoke run serves as the test-of-the-test. Assertions are fail-loud: any routing mismatch is a hard failure with a clear message. The literal-keyword (обсуди/discuss-stays-Standard) hard assertion is intentionally deferred — adding it now would be red because the current router escalates literal discuss — and is moved to a follow-up gated on the router change that makes literal discuss route to Standard (not on ATOM_004, which is only fixture hygiene). This satisfies the contract's reuse-only, atomic (1 file / 1 verifiable change / own test), ParseFile+smoke, and fail-loud requirements.

red_team_findings.what: The decision deliberately drops the task's HEADLINE deliverable. The task title and ATOM_003 spec both require asserting 'plan-refinement DISCUSS without explicit high-stakes marker stays Standard', and the atom's acceptance is 'The test fails on over-eager escalation'. The decision substitutes a keyword-FREE fixture that hits the trivial default-Standard path (decision-depth.ps1:100). Because that fixture contains none of the обсуди/discuss/approach/strategy triggers, the assertion passes regardless of whether the router over-escalates real DISCUSS tasks — it can never 'fail on over-eager escalation'.
red_team_findings.why: success_tests #4 ('correctly asserts depth-routing behavior as per ATOM_003 fail-loud direction') and the atom's own acceptance criterion are NOT met. The test provides zero regression coverage for the exact behavior ATOM_003 was created to lock down; it is a hollow test that reads as coverage but tests nothing about the DISCUSS→Standard path.

red_team_findings.what: The TDD/coverage chain is broken. ATOM_004 (the router narrowing) has acceptance 'ATOM_003 tests pass' and depends_on ATOM_003. But the hollowed keyword-free Standard fixture routes to Standard BOTH before and after ATOM_004's change, so ATOM_004's behavior change ships with no test that actually exercises it. The real assertion is pushed to an uncreated 'follow-up task gated on the router change' — i.e. a third, non-existent task.
red_team_findings.why: The router narrowing (the actual behavior the operator cares about) will land unverified. The 'fail-loud' intent of the whole atom wave is defeated: at no point in this sequence does a fail-loud assertion guard the DISCUSS-stays-Standard behavior.

red_team_findings.what: The Standard-fixture constraints are under-specified and can route to the WRONG pole. (a) If the keyword-free fixture is < 40 trimmed chars it routes Simple, not Standard (decision-depth.ps1:95) — a short 'Refine the backlog list' style string fails the assertion. (b) The step-3 keyword set (line 89) is far broader than the decision acknowledges — it includes approach/подход, strategy/страте, redesign, 'whether to', 'как лучше', 'следует ли' — all natural in plan-refinement prose. The decision only warns about обсуди/discuss/architecture, missing both the ≥40-char floor and these extra triggers.
red_team_findings.why: An implementer following the decision's stated guidance can easily produce a fixture that routes Simple or Deep, yielding a red smoke run — or, worse, the fixture gets quietly tuned until green, hardening a test that asserts nothing meaningful.

red_team_findings.what: The decision is presented as the FINAL/accepted answer, yet three of its four open_questions are load-bearing and unresolved: the exact return shape, the exact pole casing, and whether a keyword-free input deterministically routes Standard. All three are directly resolvable from decision-depth.ps1 (hashtable with .depth; casing 'Standard'/'Deep'/'High-Stakes'; keyword-free ≥40 chars → Standard), but the decision finalized without obtaining them.
red_team_findings.why: Finalizing routing-equality assertions while the equality contract is still an open question means the 'final' assertions may be wrong on first execution (e.g. comparing the whole hashtable to a string, or wrong casing). The decision asserts low risk on facts it never confirmed.

red_team_findings.what: The mitigation for the deferred assertion — 'a follow-up task must be created' — has no concrete mechanism. The implementation_plan step is merely 'record a follow-up task' with no backlog target, ID, or gating reference, and the decision output is only a code diff.
red_team_findings.why: If the follow-up is not actually recorded anywhere, the 'temporary coverage gap' becomes permanent and silent. The deferral's only stated safeguard is unenforceable, so the central behavior may never get its fail-loud assertion.

red_team_findings.what: The decision's placement risk-mitigation ('mitigated by appending it next to the current depth-routing checks') rests on a false premise: the target file has NO existing depth-routing checks. Every current assertion runs through Invoke-SynthesisPipeline with an explicit -Depth (lines 170, 189, 213); Get-SynthesisDepthDecision is never called in the test file today.
red_team_findings.why: Indicates the decision was finalized without confirming the file's contents (consistent with the unresolved return-contract open question). The new block will be a standalone first-of-its-kind section, not an append to a sibling — minor, but the stated mitigation is vacuous.

red_team_findings.what: Two spec constraints are silently unaddressed: (1) success_test #1 ('exactly one verifiable change') and #2 ('A new, dedicated test case', singular) vs. the decision's three Assert-True cases framed as 'one block'; (2) ATOM_003's declared depends_on ['ATOM_010b'] in refined-atom-list.json, which the decision never mentions even though it accepts ATOM_003 as a starting atom.
red_team_findings.why: The 'one block = one change' reading is defensible but is an operator-judgment call (success_test #6) the decision pre-empts; and dropping a declared dependency without justification leaves an ordering question open, even if ATOM_010b is plausibly spurious for a test-only atom.
